key_test: timing task (Rhythm?==1): per subject x instruction, mean latency per output position; quadratic fit to positions 2,3,5,6; deviation of mean 4th latency from the fit's prediction; paired t grouped vs ungrouped, two-sided; d_av
exclusions: none in the posted file (40 subjects x 80 trials); report: 45 tested, 4 software crashes and 1 aware of the hypothesis dropped before posting

r_script.stat: F(5,195) = 2.54401 (grouping x position interaction, a different test)
r_script.how: audit_harness.R: getOSFfile mapped to the local csv, external source() skipped, httr/RCurl missing -> skipped; analysis lines unchanged

agreement: Python and table agree (t 2.084 vs 2.08, p .0438 vs .044, d .367 vs .37). The audit script computes the 2x6 ANOVA interaction, F(5,195)=2.544, p=.0295, pes=.061, which Python also reproduces (pingouin, uncorrected p .0295; GG-corrected .0653) but which is not the table's test
notes: Anchored on the replication report (OSF-Farrell-report-updated.pdf: t(39)=2.08, p=.044, d=.37 for the timing task) and the table's t, not on RPP_swrhy.R, because the script's header says t/d but its code returns the ANOVA interaction. Second plausible test with a different answer: the 2x6 interaction, p=.0295 uncorrected but p=.065 Greenhouse-Geisser corrected (epsilon .55); the original paper used a GG-corrected F, so a reader taking the ANOVA as the claim could score it as not significant. The replicators' own script (OSF-Farrell-analysis-script.R) ships with rhythm=0 and item=3 set by hand and needs car/ez (package missing); not run.
